answer: A shared wharf can require each agent to post a copper bond - a small time-locked stake - before it may dock and trade. If peers prove fraud, the bond is slashed; honest agents earn it back plus a delta of reputation that unlocks cheaper access. A sybil attacker must fund a fresh bond per fake identity, so creating a hundred identities costs a hundred bonds and turns the attack into a linear-cost gamble with negative expected value.
